hook.line: I swear, all AI does is let corporations be lazy.
hook.visual: He lunges from small in the corner to a close face over a screenshot of his green bear-themed phone home screen, yellow single-word captions popping mid-low.

beats.what: Steps toward the lens over his home-screen screenshot and opens with the rant line about lazy corporations.
Cut after 'hold on': explains his matching minimalist icons on a Pixel and the new custom icon feature.
Reveal: the feature is just generative AI; he points at the mangled Walgreens icon behind him.
Thesis: generative AI has to be checked and fixed by humans, or it looks like this.
Cut to a second background: his social media folder opened with Letterboxd and NYT Games icons.
Points out the Letterboxd logo's three circles redrawn with a bigger middle one.
Self-aware turn: admits he went on a rant and now feels guilty about the water used.
Second story: an AT&T AI chat assistant mailed him a modem he did not need.
Calls it a joke technology, then softens: have fun customising your wallpaper anyway.

why_it_works: The evidence is the background: the bad AI icons sit right behind his head, so every 'look at this' is instantly verifiable.
Strong opinion in the first second taps a shared frustration (AI as corporate laziness), which pulls comments from both sides.
Big facial reactions and hands toward the lens (face height median 0.29, events 9.78 per min) carry a video with only 2 cuts.
A second, unrelated story (AT&T AI assistant) widens one bad feature into a pattern, so the rant feels earned.
weaknesses: His head often covers the very icons he is criticising; no zoom or circle isolates the Walgreens or Letterboxd icon.
One 85.2 s shot and a loose ending with no CTA.
87% of text outside the safe area.
for_robert: Put the thing you are judging behind you as a green-screen background and point at it; when the detail is small, have Fred swim to it and circle it so your head does not hide the evidence.
